title: Upper bound on the real part of a Fourier coefficient
statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$, with lift $\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_k^{f(x)}$ where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. Then for every frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, the real part of the Fourier coefficient of $\widetilde{f}$ at $s$ is bounded above by
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\mathrm{dist}(f,\chi_s),
\]
where $\chi_s(x) = s\cdot x$ is the linear character and $\mathrm{dist}(f,\chi_s)$ is the fraction of inputs $x$ on which $f(x) \ne s\cdot x$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function from Z_k^n to Z_k
s is a frequency in Z_k^n
replaced:
For $k \ge 2$ and $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$, the real part of
the $s$-th Fourier coefficient of the lifted function $\widetilde{f}$ satisfies
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\cdot\mathrm{dist}(f,\chi_s).
\]
